title: Bundle: per-value BitPacking select for sparse filtered scans + exact BF up to 2^27 bits at 1024 bits/key
summary:
I added a BitPacking `select` callback and a medium exact-BF tier. The tree builds, results match on every query I tested, and the bench is about 12% faster overall (geomean -11.6%), with q05 at about -21%.

**Part 1: BitpackingSelect (src/storage/compression/bitpacking.cpp, registered with `bitpacking.select = BitpackingSelect<T>`)**
- If more than 1/4 of the rows pass, it decodes the full vector with the existing BitpackingScanPartial, then compacts the selected values in place (sel is ascending, so this is safe).
- Otherwise it walks the metadata groups the same way ScanPartial does and handles each mode on its own:
  - CONSTANT writes the constant.
  - CONSTANT_DELTA computes for + delta*offset with the same unsigned wrapping as ScanPartial.
  - FOR with 4- or 8-byte T and width ≤ 56 reads each selected value straight from the LSB-first fastpforlib bitstream. It memcpys only the bytes it needs (never past the block), then shifts, masks and adds the frame of reference with unsigned wrap.
  - FOR with any other width or type unpacks only the 32-value blocks that contain a selected row, reusing the last decoded block.
  - DELTA_FOR unpacks every block in the range, as Skip does (the prefix sum needs it), and copies out the selected values.
- After each chunk the scan state advances by the rows consumed.

**Part 2: exact bitmap BF tier (src/execution/operator/join/physical_hash_join.cpp, TrySetExactBloomFilter)**
- A build now gets an exact bitmap when its key range is below min(2^27, count*1024).
- The 2^27 cap applies to every build size (the multiplication saturates once count ≥ 2^17).
- The 128 bits/key rule, the 2^22 floor and the 2^32 guard are unchanged.

**Correctness check:** I made a file-backed table with forced bitpacking (`ATTACH '/tmp/x.db' (READ_WRITE)` plus CHECKPOINT). It has BIGINT values with NULLs and widths 1 to 63, INT with mixed widths, sorted and noisy columns (DELTA_FOR / CONSTANT_DELTA), a constant column, SMALLINT, HUGEINT, UBIGINT with NULLs, and DECIMAL. I compared `sum(hash(all cols))` and `count` between a pushed filter (`a < X`) and a non-pushed one (`a+0 < X`). They matched at 0.01%, 0.5%, 5%, 24%, 30% and 2.7% (a modulo filter), and with a NULL predicate.

**Micro, warm (5 extra lineitem columns):** 5% pass went from 88–95ms to 75ms, and 0.5% pass from 94–95ms to 53ms. With count(*) alone the scan takes 26ms.

**Full bench:**

| query | change |
|---|---|
| q05 | -21.9% |
| q14 | -23.4% |
| q17 | -33.4% |
| q08 | -17.0% |
| q19 | -15.6% |
| q16 | -14.6% |
| q02 | -9.5% |
| q09 | -6.9% |
| q03 | -6.2% |
| q18 | +2.2% |
| others | noise |
| **geomean** | **-11.6%** |

**Rerun of six queries:**

| query | change |
|---|---|
| q05 | -21.2% |
| q14 | -29.7% |
| q17 | -17.3% |
| q13 | -8.4% |
| q09 | -2.0% |
| q18 | -4.6% |
| **geomean** | **-14.4%** |

I did not separate how much each part contributes; both are in the measured tree. I also did not take the warm JSON profile of lineitem scan CPU in q05 and q09 that the plan asked for.
notes:
- The earlier "BitPacking select, no gain" result was down to its design: it skipped whole 32-value blocks, and at 5% pass most blocks still hold a selected row. Reading each selected value from the bitstream is what makes the cost scale with selectivity.
- TEMP tables are never compressed (pragma_storage_info shows Uncompressed), and `ATTACH ':memory:' (COMPRESS)` fails in read-only mode. To test compressed storage, use `ATTACH '/tmp/file.db' AS m (READ_WRITE)` with `SET force_compression='bitpacking'` and `CHECKPOINT m`.
- Correlated scalar subqueries do not push filters down to the scan, so test with literal filters.
- I have not measured how much each part contributes; turning Part 2 off and re-running the bench would show it.
- Follow-ups:
  - The 1/4 density threshold was not tuned.
  - Other codecs without a select callback (ALP, Chimp/Patas, Dictionary/FSST strings) could get the same treatment.
  - The 5% micro case still costs about 50ms above count(*), so the per-value extraction loop could be optimized further.
  - Validity stored as Roaring has no select callback, so nullable columns fall back to the old path.
